narrative.overview: XionTechs is named for Mount Zion, the legendary mountain of Jerusalem, and the landing page is a climb up it. It opens at night at base camp: a Three.js Mount Zion made of white particle dots under stars. The hill is not invented; it is the real SRTM relief of Mount Zion and the valleys around it (see the 3D spec). An amber dawn glows behind the ridge and a glacier-blue rim light catches the lower slopes. Chips mark the camps where the team lives, Dallas, TX and Ho Chi Minh City. As the visitor scrolls, the camera climbs toward the summit and dawn breaks. A curved atmospheric limb, glacier blue with an amber sunrise line, hands the page to snow-white daylight. From there the page alternates daylight and night bands like weather on a mountain. An altimeter in the corner counts the climb in meters. The last night section is the summit, where the visitor names their project. The footer closes in daylight with the wordmark at mountain scale.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous story: night, dawn, daylight, dusk, summit, daylight.
One real mountain: Mount Zion, from elevation data, in 3D, as contours, and as the ridge silhouette. The altimeter reads its real metres, 602 to 765.
The name teaches itself: /siː.ɒn.teks/ hangs under the wordmark, and the footer closes with a dictionary entry.
Saira at 125% width, uppercase, carries every heading. Host Grotesk carries prose. Martian Mono carries every control, label, and reading.
Flat surfaces and 1px hairlines. No shadows, no cards with depth, no glass.
Pills for controls, a 2px radius for chips, square for everything else.
Motion is scrubbed to scroll or answers a gesture. The only things that loop are the 3D scene, the map beacons, and the route arcs, and only while on screen.
Every interactive element answers the pointer: a letter scramble, an amber fill, a cell tint, or a cursor state.

rules.name: The Dawn Rule
rules.body: Full-bleed night and daylight never meet at a straight edge. Night to daylight goes through a dawn limb (a snow dome rising from below, glacier band, amber sunrise). Daylight to night goes through a dusk limb (a night dome rising under a white or ice sky). Bands inside a section, like the service track under the giant type, may cut hard: they are ground, not sky.

rules.name: The Limb-Never-Fades Rule
rules.body: A horizon moves; it never fades. Snow faded over night at partial opacity reads as grey mud (measured #252933 → #D8D9DB on the first build). A limb rises or sets as a whole (the hero dawn is `yPercent 100 → 0` at full opacity) so the saturated glacier band always leads.

rules.name: The Amber Ration Rule
rules.body: At rest, amber covers at most about 5% of any viewport: one headline line, beacons, a route, a few links. It floods a surface only as a response: the hover fill of a filled button, or the focus fill of a chip.

rules.name: The No-Amber-On-Snow Rule
rules.body: Amber is never text or a thin rule on white (1.6:1). On daylight, amber appears only in these forms:

rules.name: The Placeholder Is Loud Rule
rules.body: Anything the user must still supply (case write-ups, testimonials) carries the Pending mono tag. A placeholder that looks finished is a fabrication.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Rule
rules.body: Every H2 is two statements: a dim line (`.tt-a`) and an ink line (`.tt-b`), each `display:block`.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Machine Rule
rules.body: Mono is only for what you press or read as data: buttons, the menu, chips, clocks, coordinates, altitude, vertical speed, counters' labels, legal and pending tags. Paragraphs are never mono.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Is-Display Rule
rules.body: Uppercase belongs to Saira headings and mono labels. Body text is always sentence case.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes in place (clocks, altitude, V/S, figures, the loader counter) uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so digits never jitter.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No element casts a box shadow. To lift, a surface changes field (snow to ice, night to night band) or gains a hairline. The one box-shadow in the system is a 1px amber underline on a focused field, and it is a rule, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Light-Is-Depth Rule
rules.body: Glow belongs to light sources in the world: the dawn behind the ridge, the glacier limb, the beacons. It is never a halo around a UI element.

rules.name: The IPA-Needs-Its-Own-Face Rule
rules.body: Saira, Host Grotesk, and Martian Mono lack ɒ and ː. Set the whole pronunciation in Noto Sans Mono, never glyph by glyph; never uppercase or scramble IPA.

dos: Do drive every scroll-linked scene with GSAP ScrollTrigger `scrub: true`, `ease: "none"`, under a Lenis instance at `lerp: 0.1` synced through `gsap.ticker`. Create pinned triggers before the triggers below them.

Do run entrances from an already-visible default: set hidden states in JS only, and ease with expo.out over 1.0–1.2s. Vary the entrance per section: mask rise (hero), rise (intro copy), wipe (stats), clip rise (cases), blur (chips), scrub fill (headlines).
Do keep reduced-motion users on native scroll: no preloader, no pins, no cursor, no scramble, final states visible, counters at their true values.
Do put `scene.background` on the Three.js scene, not only the clear color. The bloom pass restores the clear color outside a render target and double-encodes the night to #1C324D.
Do keep the render loop gated: it runs only while the hero or the summit is on screen and the tab is visible.
Do pass every full-bleed night and daylight change through a horizon limb (the Dawn Rule).
Do keep amber at or under 5% of a resting viewport (the Amber Ration Rule).
Do tag every placeholder with the Pending mono tag until the user supplies the real content.
Do clip sections whose decoration bleeds past the grid (`overflow-x: clip` on the summit, for its copy scrim). A pseudo-element 25% wider than the viewport once pushed the mobile MENU off-screen.
Do keep a physical trace of the mountain in every scene (particles, dot ridge, contours, dot map): the page is one climb, not a stack of type slides.
donts: Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a heading. UC's "ONE OPERATOR" was deliberately not carried over.
Don't set amber text or thin amber rules on snow.
Don't use box shadows, glass or blur panels, or gradient text at rest.
Don't lift the night into pale blue haze or wash the palette toward pastel. The soft rewrite of 2026-09-29 was rejected for exactly that.
Don't animate layout properties (margin, padding, width, height) outside the FAQ panel height tween. Use transforms, clip-path, opacity, and filter.
Don't tween transforms with GSAP on elements whose position depends on the CSS `translate` property (map chips, 3D chips). GSAP inlines `translate: none`.
Don't invent claims: no client logos, per-case metrics, pricing, certifications, or testimonials.
Don't use mono for prose or uppercase for body text.
Don't fade a horizon limb (the Limb-Never-Fades Rule).
Don't give a card or list item an icon that carries no meaning.
